body: Class bodies are already strict mode code, so whatever rule that's telling you that you need a use strict directive is broken.
It's the new `strict` rule that's telling me to use strict mode.
Yes, it seems the [current strict rule](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/2ce95aaae22c818030eab1485f45656aa3c4bef6/lib/rules/strict.js) doesn't mention classes anywhere at all.
@dar5hak can you provide the complete output from ESLint in both cases you describe?

`ClassDeclaration` and `ClassExpression` are always strict mode automatically, by [spec](http://www.ecma-international.org/ecma-262/6.0/#sec-strict-mode-code). so the `"use strict"` directive is unnecessary. It's correct.

But `4:13  error    Missing "use strict" statement  strict` is strange...

@dar5hak thanks. :)

So this looks like a bug in the `strict` rule. You should disable `no-extra-strict` as that is deprecated and not needed if you're using `strict`.

I will try to fix this.

I will make two PR, for `master` and for `0.x`.

And I will add a message for a reason of unnecessary: such as `module codes are strict mode always` and `class bodies are strict mode always`.
@mysticatea No need to do two PRs, do one PR into master, and we will cherry-pick that commit into 0.x branch whenever we will do a release.
Hm, this rule at 0.x has a deprecated mode which is nothing at master. So I guess two PRs are needed.
Oh, right, I forgot about deprecated mode, sorry. In that case, yes, we would probably need 2 PRs.
I'd just fix this on master. I'm doing the first RC today, and I'd rather not complicate things with continuing to do 0.x releases.

issue.body:
- I followed [this comment](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/2977#issuecomment-121651016), I set `fixes` label.
- I found lacking a check of `ArrowFunctionExpression` on `never` mode and `global` mode, so added those.
- I separated a logic for inside of modules. In this case, all `use strict` directive are unnecessary.
- I added a class support.
- I improved messages of unnecessary.
